ground_truth.description: _claimFees() sweeps the entire balance of `token0`/`token1` after `collectFees()`, stealing rewards if `rewardToken` matches `token0` or `token1`. Impact: Bribe contract receives staking rewards instead of fees.
ground_truth.root_cause: _claimFees() sweeps the entire balance of `token0`/`token1` after `collectFees()`, stealing rewards if `rewardToken` matches `token0` or `token1`. Impact: Bribe contract receives staking rewards instead of fees.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: A test deposits 10 HYBR rewards, adds 0.1 HYBR fees, and `claimFees()` sweeps all 10.1 HYBR to the bribe contract.
ground_truth.fix_description: Transfer only the difference in balance before/after `collectFees()`; add access control to `claimFees`. Status: Mitigation confirmed.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The _claimFees() function sweeps the entire balance of token0 and token1 from the contract after calling collectFees(). If the rewardToken matches either token0 or token1 of the pool, this function will inadvertently transfer staking rewards (deposited via notifyRewardAmount) to the internal_bribe contract instead of only transferring the collected fees. The function uses balanceOf(address(this)) to determine amounts to transfer, which includes any pre-existing balances of these tokens, not just the fees collected from the pool.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Assume rewardToken is the same as token0 (e.g., HYBR token). 2. DISTRIBUTION calls notifyRewardAmount() depositing 10 HYBR as staking rewards into the gauge. 3. Users generate 0.1 HYBR in trading fees in the pool. 4. Anyone calls claimFees() - the function calls collectFees() which adds 0.1 HYBR to the contract. 5. The function then reads balanceOf(address(this)) which returns 10.1 HYBR (rewards + fees). 6. All 10.1 HYBR is transferred to internal_bribe, stealing the 10 HYBR staking rewards meant for liquidity providers.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The claimFees() function is publicly callable by anyone without any access control. While the function is intended to transfer fees to the internal_bribe contract, allowing anyone to trigger this at any time could lead to timing manipulation or front-running scenarios. Combined with the balance sweep issue, this amplifies the impact as any attacker can trigger the theft of staking rewards.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. An attacker monitors the mempool for notifyRewardAmount transactions. 2. When rewards are deposited, the attacker immediately calls claimFees(). 3. This triggers the sweep of all token balances including the just-deposited rewards. 4. The attacker doesn't directly profit but causes loss to legitimate stakers by redirecting their rewards to the bribe contract.

prediction.overall_explanation: The GaugeCL contract contains a logic error in the _claimFees() function that can result in staking rewards being stolen and redirected to the internal_bribe contract. The vulnerability occurs when the rewardToken matches either token0 or token1 of the pool. The function sweeps the entire balance of these tokens rather than only the fees collected from collectFees(). This means any staking rewards held in the contract will be incorrectly transferred to the bribe contract. The issue is exacerbated by the lack of access control on claimFees(), allowing anyone to trigger this at any time. The fix requires tracking balances before and after fee collection to transfer only the actual fees, plus adding appropriate access control.
